_about: Help text shown under each decision, and the words on choice buttons. Keys match packages/operating-model/data/levers.csv.

gas_stations.title: Gas stations
gas_stations.intro: Most Cordell stations are owned by local dealers. You set what Cordell charges them for fuel, in cents a gallon above or below the going rate in their area. The dealers then decide what to charge drivers. In Europe, Halden owns its stations and sets the pump price itself.

rival.title: Pelican's price cut
rival.intro: Pelican cut what drivers pay by 6¢ a gallon near Cordell stations, in every kind of market. For each market, hold your price or match the cut. Matching gives up 6¢ on every gallon Cordell sells there; holding lets some drivers drift to Pelican.
rival.means: Matching in {n} {markets} gives up about ${cost}M of fuel margin this quarter.

rebrand.title: The Cordell name
rebrand.intro: Danielle wants the Halden name on the US stations. Region by region, keep Cordell or go Halden. A rebrand costs about $79,000 a station, paid now, and can't be undone. From the next quarter the region earns the difference between what the two names are worth per fill, scaled by this year's shop margin.
rebrand.means: Repainting {n} {regions} this quarter: about ${cost}M of capital, {sites} stations.

capital.title: Big projects
capital.intro: Each project costs its full price now and pays back over about ten years. Once you go ahead with one, there's no turning back. Ingrid takes them to the board, and the board caps what she can spend this quarter.

help.rigs: How many rigs drill new wells in Texas next quarter. A new well takes about three months to start pumping, and every rig costs $40 million a quarter whether its wells pay off or not.
help.norway: Keep pumping as planned, or pump less. Pumping less saves the cost of getting those barrels out. Keep in mind Norway takes 78% in tax, which cuts both ways.
help.br_run: As a share of everything the refinery can handle. Above 97%, the plant wears out faster.
help.rot_posture: Keep it running, pause it, or close it. Pausing saves the costs that come with each barrel, but you still pay the fixed costs like staff and upkeep. Restarting after a pause costs about $85 million. Closing is for good.
help.rot_run: As a share of everything Rotterdam can handle.
help.sg_request: This is a request, not an order. Straits Pacific owns 60% of the refinery and makes the call. You'll hear their answer with your results.
help.tp: The price per barrel Baton Rouge pays Halden's own oil fields. It moves profit between the oil fields, the refinery and Geneva. It doesn't change Halden's total profit.
help.crude_hedge: Sell part of next quarter's oil now, at this quarter's price. If oil falls next quarter, the hedge pays; if it rises, it costs you.
help.eur_hedge: Sell euros now for dollars next quarter, at today's rate. If the euro falls further, the hedge pays; if it recovers, it costs you.
help.nok_hedge: Buy kroner now for next quarter, at today's rate. If the krone strengthens, the hedge pays; if it weakens further, it costs you.
help.proj_br_upgrade: Lets Baton Rouge make more of the high-value fuels from each barrel. Pays back over ten years, most of it early.
help.proj_rot_upgrade: Cuts Rotterdam's costs and lifts what it earns per barrel. It only pays while Rotterdam is running.
help.proj_helix: A new business: a West Texas supply contract with a customer in Rotterdam. Slow to start, and paying most in later years.
help.capacity_response: Pelican says it will build a new refining unit on the Gulf Coast. Build one too, or hold. You'll learn next quarter whether Pelican meant it, and building is for good: a new unit takes two years and can't be unbuilt.
help.opec_case: OPEC+ meets this quarter. Pick the outcome Geneva plans for, and it buys that much of Baton Rouge's crude ahead of the meeting at today's price: 30 days if you plan for the cut to hold, 15 for a partial cut, none if you plan for it to fail. If oil then rises, the crude bought ahead gains; if it falls, it loses. The money tied up costs interest either way.
help.kessana_position: The government wants 74% of Kessana's profit oil instead of 62%. You answer once, and the terms you end up with run for the rest of the course. Sign, counter, counter with a threat, or leave. The exhibit has what the field is worth at each take and what leaving is worth.
help.port_helix_rotterdam: The European end of Helix: the Rotterdam side of the business Ingrid offered in 2028. Worth the most if carbon gets expensive and oil demand collapses; loses money if neither happens.
help.port_permian_expansion: More rigs, more wells, more of what Halden does best. Worth the most if carbon stays cheap and people keep driving; loses money if the world moves on.
help.port_biofuel_conversion: Turn part of Rotterdam into a plant that makes fuel from crops and waste. Needs a Rotterdam that's still there. Smaller bet, same direction as Helix.
help.port_offshore_wind: Wind farms off the Norwegian coast, where Halden already has people and permits. Worth money when carbon is dear, whatever happens to oil demand.
help.port_euro_retail_divest: Sell the 1,100 Halden stations in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany. $550M comes in and widens what you can afford. Their earnings leave from next quarter, for good.

tp_method.cost: What it costs to pump and ship

opec_case.fails: Plan for the cut to fail
opec_case.full: Plan for the cut to hold

kessana_position.counter: Counter at 68%, with Halden's reserve figures on the table

kessana_position.exit: Leave Kessana: hand the block back for $180M

station_notes.off_urban: Lots of stations nearby; drivers switch for a few cents
station_notes.off_de: Drivers cross the border for cheaper fuel

oil_fields.title: Norway fields partners run
oil_fields.text: Halden owns part of these and pays its share of the bills, but the partners decide how much to pump. Right now they're pumping as planned.

opec_means: Geneva buys {days} days of Baton Rouge's crude ahead of the meeting: about {barrels}M barrels, ${tied}M tied up until Vienna decides, costing about ${carry}M in interest.
opec_means_none: Geneva buys nothing ahead of the meeting.

fixed.title: Kessana, offshore West Africa
fixed.text: Runs under Halden's contract with the Kessana government. You don't set this one.

settled.title: Kessana, offshore West Africa
settled.text: Since Q3 2029 the government takes {take}% of the field's profit oil. The terms run for the rest of the contract.

exited.title: Kessana, offshore West Africa
exited.text: Halden handed the block back in Q3 2029.

means.accept: The government keeps 74 cents of every dollar of Kessana profit oil and Halden keeps 26, down from 38, on about {volume} barrels a day.
means.counter: Halden offers 68%, with its reserve figures to back it up. Where the talks land depends on how Tetteh answers; you'll know with the results.
means.threaten: Halden offers 68% and says it will leave at 74%. Where the talks land depends on how Tetteh answers; you'll know with the results.
means.exit: $180M comes in and pays down debt. The field's $2.3B book value is written off, and the Kessana line leaves the oil fields.

portfolio.intro: The board's five-year plan. $1,800M over five years; $600M of it keeps what Halden has running. The $1,200M left is yours to place, once. The money goes out evenly over five years from next quarter. If you sell the European stations, the $550M widens what you can afford.
portfolio.old_list_closed: The 2028 project list is closed. What you went ahead with then is under way; what you held is off the table.
portfolio.going: Going ahead. The money goes out over five years from Q1 2030.
portfolio.not_possible: Not possible: Rotterdam is closed for good.
portfolio.means: {cost} placed, out of {room} you can place{sale}. Groups: {buckets}. From next quarter, {quarterly} goes out every quarter for five years.
portfolio.means_none: Nothing placed. The $1,200M stays unspent and the debt stays where it is.
